conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. I’m Dr. Lee, one of the surgical team. You’re here today for your gastric bypass surgery, correct?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s right. I’ve been preparing for this for a long time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see from your chart you’ve struggled with weight for years and tried programs like Weight Watchers.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I’ve lost weight before, but it always comes back. I want to be healthier for my family.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s completely understandable. Your BMI is 40, which qualifies as class III obesity, and surgery can be very effective.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I also have sleep apnea and acid reflux. I hope this helps with those too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It very likely will. Many patients see improvement in both conditions after bypass.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That would be a big relief. I use CPAP every night.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll monitor your progress closely. Right now, we’re going to get you prepped for surgery. Any questions before we start?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I think I’m ready. Just a little nervous.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s completely normal. You’re in good hands. We’ll see you after the procedure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi again. You’re back in your room. The surgery went very well — laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and an endoscopy. You tolerated everything well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good to hear. I feel groggy, but okay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll be on a pain pump for now — Dilaudid PCA — so you can control your discomfort.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I be able to eat soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not yet. Tomorrow we’ll start with clear liquids — that’s stage one. We’ll advance slowly to make sure there’s no leak.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes sense.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Better. My pain is manageable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. We did an upper GI study this morning with contrast, and there’s no sign of a leak or blockage. That’s excellent news.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, that’s a relief. Can I start drinking now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll start with clear liquids — water, broth, apple juice — in small amounts. That’s stage one.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: How long will I stay on that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Usually a day or two. We’ll move you to pureed foods next, then soft solids. You’ll be on stage three by discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. What about my regular medications?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll resume them, but you’ll need to crush all pills for now — your stomach is smaller and can’t handle whole tablets.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Even my antidepressant and Abilify?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, all of them — citalopram, Abilify, lorazepam, and your pantoprazole for reflux. We’ll make sure they’re crushed and mixed with soft food.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing really well. We’re advancing your diet to stage three today — soft foods like mashed potatoes and scrambled eggs.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That sounds good. I’m hungry but trying to go slow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. Small, frequent meals — about ½ cup at a time. And no straws or gum — that can cause bloating.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I didn’t know that. Why no straws?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: They can make you swallow air, which leads to bloating and discomfort. It’s best to avoid them for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good to know. Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news — you’re cleared to go home today. You’ve tolerated stage three diet, your incisions are dry, and you’re walking well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What do I need to do when I get home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Stay on the stage three diet until your follow-up. Crush all pills, take your new meds — Protonix for reflux, Actigall for your gallbladder, and Colace for constipation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the pain medicine?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Roxicet as needed, but don’t drive or operate machinery — it can make you drowsy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll have my sister help me at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good idea. Also, no heavy lifting over 10 pounds for six weeks. You can shower, but no baths or swimming yet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And if something goes wrong?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call us or go to the ER if you have a fever over 101.5, severe pain, vomiting, or redness around your incisions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll watch for that. Thank you for everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. You did great. Follow up with Dr. Evans in two weeks. Take care.
